business_patterns.top_pattern: CT PPO spend is concentrated at Yale New Haven Hospital
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient acute hospital spend in CT PPO
key_driver_codes: YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
Vaginal Delivery without Sterilization or D&C with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: CT PPO inpatient spend rose sharply and is highly concentrated at Yale New Haven Hospital. The increase reflects both more admissions and higher paid per admission, with high-cost neurosurgical and chemotherapy-related stays adding to the pressure. A smaller secondary signal also shows more maternity volume in CT PPO acute hospitals.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: One provider is driving a disproportionate share of the increase, making this a targeted contracting and utilization management opportunity rather than a diffuse market issue.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a focused Yale New Haven Hospital review covering contract terms, inpatient level-of-care management, and authorization-to-admission controls for high-cost neurosurgical and oncology stays.
evidence_summary: CT PPO acute hospital spend increased about $17.9M, with Yale New Haven Hospital accounting for about $16.7M of that change.
At Yale New Haven Hospital, admissions rose by 176 and average paid per admission increased by about $18.3K.
Craniotomy cases added about $0.9M in CT PPO acute hospitals on 10 more admissions.
A smaller CT PPO non-authorized maternity signal added about $0.3M on 28 more admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Broad inpatient growth is pressuring HMO and PPO hospital spend
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient spend, mainly Acute Hospital and Children's facilities
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
Vaginal Delivery without Sterilization or D&C with CC
ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: Outside CT and ME, inpatient spend is rising across multiple markets through a combination of more admissions and selective unit-cost pressure. KY is the largest recurring market, while multistate HMO acute hospital growth is led by high-cost neurologic and maternity admissions. The pattern is broad enough to require standard inpatient management, but targeted enough to focus on neuro, maternity, and specific high-growth facilities.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is a repeatable inpatient cost pattern across several markets, so tightening hospital admission management and reimbursement discipline can affect a meaningful share of overall spend growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a combined UM and reimbursement action plan for KY and the multistate HMO acute-hospital markets, prioritizing neuro admissions, maternity admissions, and any facility with rising admissions plus rising paid per admit.
evidence_summary: KY HMO acute hospital spend increased about $5.9M with 196 more admissions, while KY Children's added about $1.6M on 16 more admissions.
A separate KY PPO acute hospital pattern added about $2.1M even though admissions fell by 38, because average paid per admission rose by about $15.9K.
Across CA / CO / GA / NH / NV / NY / TX, HMO acute hospital spend rose about $6.2M, led by craniotomy cases in GA (+$1.4M) and CO (+$1.3M).
A smaller CA / IN / VA HMO acute hospital utilization pattern added about $1.4M, including admissions growth at Elkhart General Hospital and additional craniotomy and maternity volume.

business_patterns.top_pattern: ME HMO acute hospital spend is being driven by admissions growth
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual HMO acute hospital spend in ME
key_driver_codes: HMO
ACUTE HOSPITAL
PA required Y
business_patterns.pattern_details: ME shows a clear utilization-led inpatient pattern. Spend increased because admissions and claims rose materially, even though paid and allowed per admission moved down. This points to a higher volume of hospital use rather than broad price escalation.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A volume-led pattern calls for admission management and referral controls, not just contract review.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit the rise in ME HMO inpatient admissions for avoidable admits, authorization conversion, and continued-stay practices before pursuing pricing changes.
evidence_summary: ME HMO acute hospital spend increased about $14.7M.
Admissions rose by 410 and claims rose by 213 in the same pattern.
Average paid per admission fell by about $36.6K, confirming that higher use, not higher unit cost, is the main driver.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization and facility mapping shifts need to be fixed before acting on several markets
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Authorization classification and facility mapping across ME, CA, GA / TX / WI, KY, CT, and IN / TX
key_driver_codes: AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION
Not Mapped
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several markets show authorization-code redistribution or facility values falling into unmapped buckets. These shifts can distort where spend appears to sit and can make real utilization or reimbursement signals look larger or smaller than they are. This is a gating validation issue and should be resolved before using these segments for policy or contracting action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If the coding or mapping is wrong, business teams may chase artificial cost movement and miss the true operational lever.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Reconcile PA-required coding and facility mapping in ME, CA, KY, CT, IN, TX, GA, and WI, then restate the affected inpatient trends before launching UM or network interventions.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The findings explicitly show authorization-code distribution shifts and unmapped facility values flagged for validation before action.
evidence_summary: ME shows an authorization-code distribution shift of about -$3.4M that requires validation before business action.
GA / TX / WI and CA show additional authorization-code distribution movement of about +$1.3M each.
KY has about +$1.2M of spend sitting in a 'Not Mapped' facility bucket, with smaller unmapped signals in CT and IN / TX.
These mapping effects touch both high-cost neuro and chemotherapy-related inpatient categories, so they can misstate authorization and site-of-care conclusions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases are creating outsized cost spikes
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual IP Med/Surg specialty inpatient episodes
key_driver_codes: Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell and Other Immunotherapies
Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System with MCC
Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with Spinal Curvature, Malignancy, Infection or Extensive Fusions with CC
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
HEMIPLG FLW CEREB INFARCT LT N-DOM
business_patterns.pattern_details: A small number of very high-cost inpatient specialty cases are creating disproportionate spend increases. The pattern includes cellular therapy, transplant, complex spinal surgery, craniotomy, and severe neurologic recovery cases, often with very few admissions but extremely high paid amounts per stay. These should be handled as case-level catastrophic reviews, not as broad population trends.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of specialty claims can materially move total spend and may require different reimbursement, stop-loss, and clinical escalation actions than ordinary inpatient growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Pull case-level reviews for these specialty admissions, confirm contract and stop-loss handling, and route transplant, cellular therapy, and catastrophic neuro/spine episodes for specialized reimbursement and clinical review.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Many of these findings are flagged as low baseline or small-number events, so case-level confirmation is needed before broad policy conclusions are drawn.
evidence_summary: In CT / IN / UNATTRIBUTED / WI, rare IP Med/Surg outliers added about $6.7M, including Yale New Haven Hospital CAR-T immunotherapy at about $2.6M on 4 more admissions.
The same outlier set includes about $2.1M from spinal fusion with device infection on 2 admissions and about $1.4M from heart transplant or heart-assist admissions on 2 admissions.
CA rare and complex craniotomy-related cases added about $4.1M, with individual diagnoses contributing roughly $0.7M to $1.0M each.
TX severe neurologic and orthopedic recovery cases added about $4.2M across stroke-related hemiplegia and musculoskeletal aftercare patterns, including one stroke-related diagnosis at about $1.4M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Spend is shifting into post-acute and alternative inpatient settings
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient spend in Long Term Care Hospital, Physical Rehab, Critical Access, and NF settings
key_driver_codes: LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL
Physical Rehab
CRITICAL ACCESS
AFTERCARE FOLLOW JNT REPLACE SURG
Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Beyond acute hospitals, a meaningful share of spend growth is moving into long-term care hospitals, physical rehab, critical access hospitals, and nursing-facility-type recovery settings. The recurring clinical themes are neurologic recovery and orthopedic aftercare, with some markets showing more admissions and others showing very high paid per admission in low-volume cases. This looks like a care-pathway and site-of-care management opportunity.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Post-acute migration can bypass acute hospital controls and create avoidable cost if discharge planning and preferred-setting rules are not aligned.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review discharge pathways for neuro and orthopedic cases, tighten preferred post-acute placement rules, and validate whether these stays should have been directed to lower-cost settings when clinically appropriate.
evidence_summary: CA EPO long-term care hospital spend increased about $0.6M on 2 more admissions, with average paid per admission up about $288.5K.
TX HMO physical rehab added about $0.4M on 20 more admissions even though paid per admission fell, pointing to more use of rehab beds.
NH / NY HMO physical rehab added about $0.3M, including a NY case with about $94.3K higher paid per admission.
CT and CA long-term care hospital patterns added about $0.6M combined, while TX critical access and NF recovery settings contributed another roughly $0.3M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: WI inpatient chemotherapy is emerging as a focused oncology cost driver
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient oncology and chemotherapy episodes in WI
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
ENCOUNTER FOR ANTINEOPLASTIC CHEMO
business_patterns.pattern_details: WI shows a focused inpatient chemotherapy pattern rather than broad inpatient inflation. The rise reflects both more chemotherapy-related admissions and higher paid per admission within the same oncology episode type. This is best addressed as an oncology pathway question, including whether some treatment intensity belongs in a different setting.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Oncology episodes usually need different clinical, utilization, and reimbursement actions than general medical-surgical admissions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review inpatient chemotherapy criteria, confirm whether these cases met inpatient necessity standards, and assess opportunities to redirect appropriate treatment to lower-cost oncology settings.
evidence_summary: WI inpatient chemotherapy-related spend increased about $1.1M.
Admissions rose by 42 and claims rose by 22 in this chemotherapy pattern.
Average paid per admission increased by about $6.4K, showing both volume and intensity pressure within the same episode type.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX maternity complexity is lifting inpatient delivery spend
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual maternity inpatient episodes in TX
key_driver_codes: Vaginal Delivery without Sterilization or D&C with CC
GEST DM CHILDBIRTH INSULIN CONTROL
OTH SPEC PREG RELATED COND 3RD TRI
MAT CARE LW TRANS SCAR PREV C/S DEL
ABN FETL HEART RATE RHYTHM COMP L&D
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX maternity spend is rising through a concentrated set of higher-complexity delivery episodes. The main drivers are gestational diabetes, other third-trimester pregnancy complications, prior C-section-related care, and fetal heart-rate complications. This is a focused obstetric case-mix pattern and should be handled separately from general inpatient management.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Maternity pathways, prior C-section management, and delivery-setting practices require different interventions than other inpatient categories.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route these TX delivery episodes to obstetric clinical review to assess care pathway consistency, prior C-section management, and whether case complexity is being captured and managed appropriately.
evidence_summary: TX maternity-focused inpatient patterns added about $1.1M in total.
Gestational diabetes in childbirth added about $0.3M on 10 more admissions, with average paid per admission up about $27.1K.
Other third-trimester pregnancy-related conditions added about $0.3M on 6 more admissions, with average paid per admission up about $42.5K.
Additional delivery complexity came from fetal heart-rate complications and prior C-section-related care.

executive_summary.headline: The dominant story is concentrated inpatient hospital growth, with a few provider- and specialty-driven patterns amplified by authorization and mapping issues that must be validated first.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: CT PPO spend is heavily concentrated at Yale New Haven Hospital, while several other markets show broader HMO and PPO inpatient growth driven by admissions and selective unit-cost pressure. Separate action paths are needed for validation issues, rare catastrophic specialty cases, post-acute site-of-care migration, inpatient oncology, and TX maternity complexity.
recommended_focus_order: Fix authorization-code and facility mapping issues before acting on affected markets.
Address concentrated hospital and multistate inpatient growth through combined UM, contracting, and provider-specific review.
Handle catastrophic specialty, post-acute, oncology, and maternity patterns through separate clinical and reimbursement workflows.

notes: Eight patterns were returned to keep provider economics, utilization, validation, site-of-care, oncology, maternity, and rare high-cost outliers separate.

Ungrouped items are lower-material residual patterns, mainly smaller GA behavioral health provider-mix findings and smaller POS/PPO acute hospital signals that did not outrank the selected business table.
Validation patterns were consolidated into one gating pattern so downstream teams do not act on potentially artificial movement before coding and mapping are reconciled.
